milestone: Guarded world-service root-prop lifecycle and live desktop snapshots
implemented: runtime.structure.transact creates frozen root-prop templates and removes previously spawned props with tick/structure guards and generated IDs in request order.
Thirty-two typed structural receipts retain successful native outcomes before response serialization; matching retries and cross-method request-ID conflicts are tested.
Native structural transactions and tick batches retain rollback journals for membership, components, physics and ID allocation; snapshot v3 preserves provenance and allocator history.
Active saves/replacements require expected_structure_revision after any topology change, independently of tick and custom component revisions.
Editor save observations, runtime polling, Scene/Game snapshot caches and queued capture guards include structural revision.
Scene and Game use the same live native geometry snapshot assembly. Camera-independent snapshots include born props, exclude retired props and preserve earlier snapshot values.

managed_editor.build: Release win-x64, pinned .NET 10.0.401, existing locked packages

prior_failures.compiler: Initial Windows compiler frontend crashed while the worktree was changing; frozen-source rebuilds passed. No compiler root-cause claim.
prior_failures.desktop: Initial unchanged graphics fixture found that the Scene snapshot still enumerated authored-only entities. Shared native live snapshot assembly fixed this; the same fixture passed.

limitations: Initial lifecycle supports root props only; originally authored entities cannot be removed. No camera/controller/rig/emitter hierarchy instantiation.
C# initiation, scheduled RPC structural commands, arbitrary component membership changes, self-reference remapping and a runtime-only hierarchy/Inspector workflow remain unfinished.
Legacy runtime mutations do not universally accept structural revision guards. Structural receipts are bounded, session-local and not durable across process restarts.
Focused AMD Vulkan owned-HWND validation at 4x MSAA; no NVIDIA rerun, full Avalonia visual review, physical input or game-performance claim.
Editor Save model compiles and native guards are tested; its new stale-observation display has not been exercised through actual widgets in this checkpoint.

No new desktop package/launcher activation. Earlier CoreCLR/NativeAOT journal and lifecycle qualification remains bound to the foundation evidence, not a new complete Windows compiled-gameplay qualification.
Portable physics saves reconstruct typed state and do not promise bit-identical future contact caches.
